readiness.title: Readiness Intelligence
readiness.subtitle: Multi-factor, explainable readiness for every person and unit — evidence-weighted and audited.
readiness.selectHint: Select an entity to see its factor breakdown.
readiness.explainNote: Readiness = CompetencyScore × EvidenceConfidence × DataQuality × RiskAdjustment × RoleCriticality × Recency, shown as the geometric mean.

governance.principle: AI recommends · Humans review · Evidence validates · Governance assures.

profiles.trustHint: Line Manager approval + HR validation together make the profile Trusted.
profiles.noResults: No competency results yet — run an assessment.

competencyDetail.calibratedNote: A competency is calibrated by role, level, experience and risk — not a fixed bar.

assessment.what: An employee's real proficiency in a competency on a 1–5 scale, scored from their own answers plus supporting evidence — with a confidence value, never a bare guess.
process: An assessor assigns the assessment for one or more competencies to the employee.
The employee is notified and completes it in their own account — multiple-choice and scenario items.
The engine auto-scores each item (MCQ: correct = 1, scenario: a 0–1 rubric score) and estimates the level.
Matching evidence is pulled in and a confidence score is computed from signal, evidence and consistency.
If confidence is below the threshold, the result is routed to a human governance review before it counts.

measure.label: Assessed level
measure.value: round(mean of item scores × 5), clamped to 1–5

measure.label: Confidence
measure.value: 0.5 × proficiency signal + 0.3 × evidence (0–3 sources) + 0.2 × consistency

measure.label: Consistency
measure.value: 1 − variance across items — how much the answers agree

measure.label: Review gate
measure.value: confidence < 0.75 → routed to human review (governance)

measure.label: Level scale
measure.value: P1 Awareness · P2 Basic · P3 Working · P4 Advanced · P5 Expert

next: Approved results update the employee's 360° profile and readiness index.
The gap (required − assessed) flows into the development plan and training.
Low-confidence results wait for a reviewer's approve / reject in Governance.

readiness.what: How ready a person is for their role right now, on a 0–100 index that fuses competency, evidence, data quality, risk, role criticality and recency.
process: Every approved competency result for the employee is collected with its confidence.
Six factors are computed and each normalized to 0–1.
They are combined as a geometric mean, so one weak factor can't be masked by strong ones.
Floors and bands then assign a readiness status.

measure.label: Index
measure.value: 100 × (competency × evidence × data-quality × risk × role-criticality × recency) ^ (1/6)

measure.label: Competency
measure.value: evidence-weighted attainment: assessed ÷ required, weighted by risk

measure.label: Recency
measure.value: 0.5 ^ (age in days ÷ 365) — evidence decays over time

measure.label: Risk adjustment
measure.value: penalty for unmet high-risk competencies, floored at 0.4

measure.label: Status bands
measure.value: ≥ 85 Ready · ≥ 70 Ready, minor gaps · else Development required

measure.label: Floors
measure.value: evidence or recency below 0.40 forces re-assessment

next: Critical-role shortfalls surface in Succession and Workforce Planning.
Insufficient evidence or a stale assessment triggers a re-assessment request.

gaps.what: The distance between the level a role requires and the level a person actually has — ranked by how risky each gap is.
process: For each competency, compare the required (target) level to the assessed (current) level.
Compute the gap and weight it by the competency's risk weight.
Sort so the most critical gaps come first.

measure.label: Gap size
measure.value: target level − current level (0–5)

measure.label: Weighted gap
measure.value: gap size × risk weight

measure.label: Priority
measure.value: weighted ≥ 3 Very high · ≥ 2 High · else Medium

measure.label: Confidence
measure.value: same model as assessment — signal + evidence + consistency

next: High-priority gaps drive the individual development plan and training assignment.
Aggregated gaps feed department and company workforce planning.

competencies.what: The shared standard: each competency, the level each job requires, and what behaviour looks like at every one of the five proficiency levels.
process: Define the competency (bilingual) and link it to professional standards.
Set the required level (P1–P5) per job, with a risk weight.
Describe each level — knowledge, skill, behaviour and the evidence expected.

measure.label: Level scale
measure.value: P1 Awareness · P2 Basic · P3 Working · P4 Advanced · P5 Expert

measure.label: Required level
measure.value: the target level a specific job demands for this competency (1–5)

measure.label: Risk weight
measure.value: multiplier (≥ 1) that raises a competency's priority in gaps and readiness

next: These requirements become the benchmark for every assessment and gap calculation.

governance.what: The human-in-the-loop gate: no AI result enters a workforce decision without review, and every consequential change is recorded in a tamper-evident log.
process: Any AI output below the confidence threshold opens a pending decision.
A reviewer sees the recommendation, its confidence and the evidence behind it.
They approve or reject — only approved results take effect.
Every action is appended to the audit hash chain.

measure.label: Trigger
measure.value: AI confidence < 0.75 → decision opened as PENDING_REVIEW

measure.label: Statuses
measure.value: PENDING_REVIEW → APPROVED or REJECTED

measure.label: Audit chain
measure.value: each entry = SHA-256(previous hash + change) — any edit breaks the chain

next: Approved results flow on to profiles, readiness and planning.
The full audit log can be re-verified end-to-end at any time.

value.what: The institutional value the platform delivers, as a single 0–100 index across six dimensions, computed from live data.
process: Each of the six dimensions is measured directly from current records.
The six scores are averaged into one value index you can track over time.

measure.label: Readiness visibility
measure.value: % of the workforce with an assessed readiness index

measure.label: Risk control
measure.value: % of critical roles not at high loss risk (≥ 0.6)

measure.label: Training ROI
measure.value: average gap-closure % across training interventions

measure.label: Succession strength
measure.value: ready people (≥ 75) ÷ critical roles, capped at 100%

measure.label: Decision speed
measure.value: % of governance decisions resolved

measure.label: Fairness & transparency
measure.value: average confidence of gap assessments

next: Track the index over time to evidence the program's impact to leadership.

dashboard.what: The organization-wide readiness picture for leadership: workforce readiness, where risk concentrates, and the value the program is creating.
process: Every employee's readiness index is aggregated across the organization.
Critical-role and low-evidence risks are surfaced.
The six-dimension value index is computed from live data.

measure.label: Workforce readiness
measure.value: distribution of 0–100 readiness indices

measure.label: Risk
measure.value: critical roles at high loss risk + low-evidence results

measure.label: Value index
measure.value: mean of the six ROI dimensions (0–100)

next: Drill from any tile into a department, role or competency.

workspace.what: Your personal readiness cockpit: your competency profile, where you stand against your role, your development path and what to do next.
process: Your approved assessment results build your competency radar.
Your readiness index and status are computed from those results.
Unmet competencies become your recommended actions and learning.

measure.label: Readiness
measure.value: 0–100 index — same engine as the executive dashboard

measure.label: Competency radar
measure.value: assessed ÷ required, per competency

measure.label: Development path
measure.value: Learn → Practice → Apply → Excel, set by readiness band

next: Open a recommended action to start closing a gap.
Completed assessments and training update this view automatically.

team.what: Your team's readiness at a glance: each member's status, their open gaps, and the approvals waiting on you.
process: Each member's readiness and gaps are rolled up from their profiles.
Critical gaps and low-confidence results are flagged for attention.
Approvals (assessments, plans) are queued for your review.

measure.label: Member readiness
measure.value: per-person 0–100 index

measure.label: Team rollup
measure.value: spread across Ready / minor gaps / development

measure.label: Approvals
measure.value: items routed to you by the workflow engine

next: Approve or return items; assign assessments or development.

dept.what: The department's readiness map: critical roles, their coverage, and succession depth across its sections.
process: Profiles in the department are aggregated by section and role.
Critical roles are matched against ready candidates.
Coverage and concentration of risk are summarized.

measure.label: Department readiness
measure.value: mean member readiness, weighted by role criticality

measure.label: Critical-role coverage
measure.value: ready candidates ÷ critical roles

measure.label: Succession depth
measure.value: candidates within reach per critical role

next: Drill into a section or role; act on uncovered critical roles.

hierarchy.what: The organizational backbone — NOC → subsidiaries → activities → departments → sections — that every record is scoped to.
process: Define org nodes and their parent–child relationships.
Bind jobs, roles and employees to nodes.
Tenancy and access then follow the tree (row-level security).

measure.label: Node
measure.value: an l1 org unit with a parent and a type

measure.label: Scope
measure.value: every tenant-scoped record carries tenant_id = a node

measure.label: Access
measure.value: the request's role + node decide what's visible (RLS)

next: Readiness, gaps and planning all roll up along this tree.

profiles.what: The verified 360° picture of each person — competencies, qualifications, certifications, experience and evidence — plus their readiness.
process: Pull the person's competency results, qualifications, certs and experience.
Validate records and weight by verification (data quality).
Compute readiness and surface remaining gaps.

measure.label: Readiness
measure.value: 0–100 index from the readiness engine

measure.label: Data quality
measure.value: share of approved / verified records

measure.label: Evidence
measure.value: records matched to competencies at similarity ≥ 0.5

next: Trusted profiles flow into succession and workforce planning.

blueprint.what: Governed assessment templates derived from the approved role-competency matrix — AI drafts the items, humans approve before use.
process: Select a role / competency set from the approved matrix.
AI drafts items (MCQ, scenario) with difficulty and expected evidence.
A reviewer approves; only approved blueprints can be assigned.

measure.label: Source
measure.value: the approved role-competency requirement matrix

measure.label: AI draft
measure.value: items via the model gateway, each with a confidence

measure.label: Gate
measure.value: human approval required before a blueprint is usable

next: Approved blueprints power assessments and campaigns.

succession.what: Ranked successors for critical roles, scored by readiness and remaining gaps, so scarce knowledge is protected.
process: List critical roles and their required competencies.
Score candidates by readiness and weighted remaining gaps.
Rank, then flag bench depth and single points of failure.

measure.label: Candidate score
measure.value: readiness (≥ 75 = ready) minus weighted remaining gaps

measure.label: Bench depth
measure.value: ready candidates per critical role

measure.label: Risk
measure.value: critical roles with no ready successor

next: Target development at near-ready candidates to deepen the bench.

training.what: Training tied to verified gaps, with before / during / after tracking and measured gap-closure.
process: A verified gap defines the learning need.
Training is assigned and moves through stages (before → during → after).
Post-training re-assessment measures the gap closure.

measure.label: Need
measure.value: from an approved gap (required − assessed)

measure.label: Stage
measure.value: BEFORE / DURING / AFTER, with % closure

measure.label: Training ROI
measure.value: average gap-closure % (feeds the value index)

next: Closure updates the person's readiness and development plan.

strategy.what: Cascade strategic objectives to the competencies that deliver them, and measure the strategic readiness gap.
process: Define objectives and cascade them down the hierarchy.
Map each objective to the competencies it depends on.
Compare required vs available competency to size the strategic gap.

measure.label: Alignment
measure.value: objectives mapped to enabling competencies

measure.label: Strategic gap
measure.value: competency required by objectives − current competency

next: Drives where to invest assessment and development.

ops.what: Sites, equipment, procedures and critical tasks — linked to the competencies that de-risk operating them.
process: Register assets, procedures and critical tasks.
Link each critical task to the competencies it requires.
Expose where operations are at risk from unmet competencies.

measure.label: Critical task
measure.value: an operation that requires specific competencies

measure.label: Exposure
measure.value: tasks whose required competencies are unmet by assigned staff

next: Operational risk feeds gap and planning priorities.

campaigns.what: Run assessments at scale: enroll participants, run attempts, score, and review results under governance.
process: Create a campaign from an approved blueprint and enroll participants.
Participants complete attempts; items are auto-scored.
Low-confidence results route to review before they count.

measure.label: Enrollment
measure.value: participants in the campaign

measure.label: Scoring
measure.value: same engine as assessment — level and confidence

measure.label: Review gate
measure.value: confidence < 0.75 → governance

next: Approved results update profiles and gaps in bulk.

devplan.what: Turn verified gaps into a development plan of concrete items, then track completion to closure.
process: Approved gaps generate learning needs.
Needs become plan items with owners and target dates.
Completion is tracked; re-assessment confirms closure.

measure.label: Source
measure.value: verified gaps (required − assessed)

measure.label: Plan item
measure.value: an action with an owner, due date and status

measure.label: Completion
measure.value: % of items done; closure confirmed by re-assessment

next: Closure raises readiness and clears the gap.

workflows.what: Configurable multi-step approvals over any entity, plus scoped permission roles.
process: Define a workflow: its steps, approvers and the entity it governs.
An action enters the workflow and routes step by step.
Each decision is recorded; final approval applies the change.

measure.label: Steps
measure.value: ordered approver stages

measure.label: Permission roles
measure.value: scoped grants deciding who can act

measure.label: Audit
measure.value: every decision appended to the audit hash chain

next: Approved changes take effect; rejected ones are returned.

aistudio.what: Every AI request is logged with its input and model version; every output carries a confidence and passes human review.
process: A request goes through the model gateway (the model is swappable).
Input, model version and output are logged.
Outputs below the threshold open a governance decision.

measure.label: Logged
measure.value: input + model version + output, per request

measure.label: Confidence
measure.value: attached to every output (0–1)

measure.label: Gate
measure.value: confidence < 0.75 → human review

next: Approved outputs flow into the relevant module.

groups.what: Build arbitrary workforce groups with a readiness rollup, and curate talent pools.
process: Define a group by any criteria, or curate a pool by hand.
Member readiness is rolled up for the group.
Pools are tracked for targeted development.

measure.label: Rollup
measure.value: distribution / mean of member readiness

measure.label: Pool
measure.value: a curated set of people for a purpose

next: Use pools to target assessment, development or succession.

wfp.what: Supply vs demand for competencies, critical-role coverage, forecasting and benchmarking — readiness turned into a plan.
process: Aggregate current competency supply across the workforce.
Compare it to demand from roles and strategy.
Forecast coverage and benchmark against targets.

measure.label: Supply
measure.value: available competency at required levels

measure.label: Demand
measure.value: competency required by roles and objectives

measure.label: Coverage
measure.value: supply ÷ demand, per critical role

next: Coverage gaps drive hiring, development and succession.

graph.what: The relationships across the platform — roles, competencies, evidence, assets and strategy — as one connected graph.
process: Entities and their links are assembled into nodes and edges.
You can traverse from any node to related ones.
Paths reveal how strategy connects to people and evidence.

measure.label: Nodes
measure.value: entities: roles, competencies, people, assets, objectives

measure.label: Edges
measure.value: typed relationships between them

next: Trace impact — e.g. which people an objective depends on.

integrations.what: Connectors to HR, LMS, ERP, CMMS, HSE and BI systems — each with an audited sync log.
process: Configure a connector and its credentials.
Sync pulls or pushes records on a schedule or on demand.
Every sync is logged for audit.

measure.label: Connector
measure.value: a typed link to an external system

measure.label: Sync log
measure.value: records moved, status and timestamp — audited

next: Synced data feeds profiles, training and evidence.

enablement.what: Onboarding and guidance to get teams using the platform — playbooks, role guides and rollout support.
process: Pick the role-based guide for your part of the rollout.
Follow the playbook steps to configure and adopt.
Track adoption and the readiness of the rollout itself.

measure.label: Guides
measure.value: role-based how-to content

measure.label: Adoption
measure.value: progress through the rollout playbook

next: Move teams from setup to active use.

diagnostic.what: A self-check of how complete each of the 10 platform layers and its documents are — what's ready, needs review, or needs building.
process: Each layer is checked against its expected entities and documents.
Status is classified Ready / Needs review / Needs build.
Gaps in the platform's own setup are surfaced.

measure.label: Status
measure.value: READY / NEEDS_REVIEW / NEEDS_BUILD, per layer

measure.label: Coverage
measure.value: expected vs present entities and documents

next: Prioritize what to configure or document next.

settings.what: Configure integrations and connections; Save & Test applies them live, with no redeploy.
process: Enter connection details for a service (e.g. SMTP, an API).
Save & Test validates and applies the change immediately.
Settings take effect live and are recorded.

measure.label: Connection
measure.value: a service config — endpoint and credentials

measure.label: Save & Test
measure.value: validates, then applies without a redeploy

next: Configured services activate features — e.g. email notifications.
